summary.en: Militant gunmen attacked a polio vaccination team in Mohmand, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, killing two policemen and wounding another. In Karachi, a PIA engineer was killed in a separate attack. Pakistani forces returned fire on Afghan Taliban posts in South Waziristan after Taliban fire on Pakistani posts, intensifying border clashes. Soaring LPG prices are forcing rickshaw drivers to cut meals, adding economic pressure on commuters. The conflict caused 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Militantvåpnede menn angrep et poliovaksinasjonsteam i Mohmand i Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, og drepte to politifolk og såret en annen. I Karachi ble en PIA-ingeniør drept i et eget angrep. Pakistanske styrker svarte med ild mot afghanske Taliban-poster i Sør-Waziristan etter at Taliban skjøt mot pakistanske poster, noe som intensiverte grensekonfliktene. Økende LPG-priser tvinger rickshaw-sjåfører til å kutte måltider, noe som legger ekstra økonomisk press på reisende. Konflikten forårsaket 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
